cohort: A nationwide study of 991 women aged 18-45 years, 6-18 months post-cesarean section, in Japan.
finding: Abnormal scar formation after cesarean section is highly prevalent (66.0%), significantly impairs maternal quality of life, and keloid formation is linked to an increased risk of postpartum depression.
mod_finding: Abnormal scar formation after cesarean section is highly prevalent and negatively impacts maternal quality of life, with keloid formation specifically increasing the risk of postpartum depression.
